video.title: You Can Feel This - Here's How

classification.reason: The coach provides actionable mental cues and physical feels for the forward swing, specifically instructing the player to intend to pull the hip backward while driving the shoulders forward.

problem.title_as_question: Should you actively fire your hip forward in the forehand, and what should you feel instead?
problem.definition: Addressing the contradiction between the pelvis rotating forward on video and how players should mentally control it, explaining why consciously firing the hip forward ruins rotational tension while cueing the hip back creates proper shoulder acceleration.
prerequisites: unit turn coiling the upper body
problem.target_player: Players trying to develop rotational power who are confused by the cue to drive the hip forward

symptoms.description: The hips and shoulders rotate forward together as a single block rather than twisting opposite to build tension.
The player cannot feel elastic stretch tension across the torso when consciously pushing the right hip through.
The pelvis slows down and stops its forward rotation as the shoulders overtake it into the forward swing.

causes.statement: Trying consciously to send the right hip forward causes the player to release trunk tension so the hips and shoulders move together without resistance.
The fascial line connecting hip and shoulder creates reciprocal tension that flings the shoulder forward while simultaneously pulling the hip backward.
The pelvis initially rotates forward dynamically to pull on the front anchor and maximize fascial stretch before the shoulders uncoil.
The pelvis undergoes backward acceleration from the stretched tissue which physically manifests as braking and deceleration rather than reversing direction.

angles.summary: The external oblique and fascial chain connect hip and shoulder, storing elastic energy when twisted in opposite directions.
A corkscrew model illustrates how pulling the front anchor forward and back anchor backward stretches the system and snaps them together upon release.
Players wrongly assume that seeing the pelvis rotate forward on video means they should consciously drive the hip forward during the swing.
The human motor control system perceives tension and acceleration rather than absolute motion, feeling the hip get yanked backward as the shoulder accelerates.

solutions.summary: Intend to take the hitting-side hip and fire it backwards during the forward swing to engage rotational tension.
When coiled and about to swing, cue yourself to drive your shoulders forward while pulling your hips back.
Feel whether your pelvis is under backward-pulling tension as your shoulder accelerates, confirming it decelerates to transfer energy.
